scope: Source-grounded proposals for the three existing T01 cases only. No runtime execution or inventory mutation.
shared_safety_precondition: Use a dedicated test OS account or test machine whose system clipboard is disposable. A disposable Chrome profile does not isolate the OS clipboard, which is shared across profiles and applications.

Do not inspect, copy, screenshot, or record the clipboard before starting. The positive setup overwrites it with the exact owned synthetic string below. Do not run these procedures in a user's ordinary OS session.

Use the already installed/available development extension artifact. Reload that existing artifact and confirm its extension identity matches the known development build before use; do not build, package, install, or change identity for this procedure. If there is no known existing development artifact, leave runtime unverified.

If no dedicated disposable OS clipboard is available, do not execute the positive case: there is no safe way to test these system clipboard handlers without changing shared OS state. Report this fixture constraint; do not treat a Chrome profile as isolation.

For each of the three cases, reload the already identified development extension, reopen Tools > Catalog, choose All handlers, locate the exact handler, and record its visible availability and displayed schema before execution. Record the declared and granted permission state relevant to that handler from the existing build/Settings > Advanced agent capabilities; do not infer runtime denial from a direct-runner failure. If reload or permission state cannot be checked safely, mark that dimension unverified with the reason.
After each reload/navigation to Settings or the runner, reselect the owned HTTPS test tab and verify it is still the focused tab immediately before Run. Never proceed on uncertain target or focus.

manual_runner.path: Tools > Catalog; select All handlers, search/open the exact handler, enter JSON in Test runner, press Run.
manual_runner.semantics: The runner parses JSON, safe-parses the local schema, then calls handler.run directly with permissionMode=act and assignedTabId=null. It bypasses dispatcher approval and role enforcement. Handler execution here does not prove dispatcher behavior, approval/denial behavior, role denial, or live tool binding. Source note: src/lib/tools/dispatch.ts:792-803 contains the optional-permission dispatcher check, while ToolsView.tsx:453-462 directly calls handler.run; therefore a manual-run failure is recorded exactly as observed and is not labeled dispatcher denial.
manual_runner.expected_target: Immediately before EVERY Run (positive, invalid, fixture setup, and cleanup), confirm the intended ordinary public HTTPS test tab is selected in the test Chrome window. Record only its owned test URL, never page content. If target or focus is uncertain, stop before Run. The manual context resolves the focused current-window tab at execution time.

limits: All runtime observations remain unverified; these are proposed source-derived procedures only.

A browser profile does not isolate the system clipboard. Safe positive execution requires a disposable OS-level clipboard context; if unavailable, the precise unresolved fixture constraint is that clipboard read/write inherently observes or changes shared OS clipboard state.
Manual Tools runner results do not establish dispatcher permission prompts, Ask/Act approval or denial, member/admin authorization, or live database binding.

Reload and permission dimensions are proposed observations, not observed evidence. Record each case separately; if either cannot be checked safely, keep that dimension unverified and state why. A direct manual-run failure is not evidence of dispatcher denial.
final_cleanup: After all clipboard cases, attempt set_clipboard with exactly {"text":""} on the dedicated disposable OS clipboard, with the owned HTTPS tab confirmed focused immediately before Run. Capture the exact result. Do not read the clipboard to verify cleanup and do not claim any prior value was restored. If cleanup fails, leave that OS account/machine out of use until the clipboard can be cleared through an owned local action; report the exact failure and that cleanup remains unverified.
